title: Release evidence is bound to criterion receipts at the released SHA, so an unattended release is decided on the same evidence goal closure demands
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 1), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168 and reproduced by probe; correctness refuter FAILED to refute; severity refuter lowered it (human-only path, preview verdict visible in the PR body). OWNER DIRECTION 2026-09-09 REFRAMES THE FIX: "we can approve the plan at the start but that's it" — moe-next must NOT add a preview-approval gate before release. So the reviewer's prescription (require an APPROVED preview via a new RELEASE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED code) is REJECTED. What remains is the reviewer's correct diagnosis: the machine evidence at release is weaker than at goal closure, and that is precisely what must be fixed BEFORE release can be auto-approved. This row is the prerequisite of the auto-approval row.

MECHANISM, measured (reviewer's line anchors did not drift):
- release-durable-facts.ts:34-53 nodeFacts reads each node's GENERAL verifier receipt (`receipt.execution.test`, one command per node) + landing receipt; :52 `sha: receipt.execution.workspaceBinding?.headSha ?? null`.
- release-dossier.ts:84-94 landingOf applies ancestry ONLY to node.landingSha; :109-111 the receipt gap fires only when receipt is null or receipt.sha is null — receipt.sha itself is NEVER ancestry-checked. So the dossier's line "Every cited commit was re-measured as an ancestor of this sha" means the landing commit is in the tree, NOT that any verifier or criterion check ran at the released tree. MEASURED: a dossier whose verifier receipt sha (999…9) is not an ancestor of HEAD (fff…f) yields gaps=0.
- release-dossier-sections.ts:14-21 DossierGapCode roster has 7 codes, none about criterion-at-sha. release-decide-service.ts:151-163 the ONLY evidence gate is releaseDossierGaps.
- grep: no non-test file under apps/daemon/src/release/ imports currentCriterionReceipts / readCriterionEvidence. Only http/document-coverage-criteria.ts and criterion-evidence/criterion-service.ts do.
- CONTRAST, the stronger seam that ALREADY EXISTS: criterion-evidence/criterion-read.ts:29-44 currentCriterionReceipts (latest run COMPLETED, sameCriterionArtifact, receipt PASSED, approved check + criterionDigest match); criterion-artifact.ts:34-61 readIntegratedCriterionArtifact binds every node landing to the integrated sha via merge-base --is-ancestor and checks verifier workspaceBinding.root; goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts:24-33 GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED consumes it. The producer is composed: criterion-runner.ts + criterion-command-edge.ts, wired at daemon-command-registry.ts:417. docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md:47 says "no composed producer yet" — that line is 3 days stale; the planning architect must re-measure whether the runner is actually TRIGGERED in the normal journey, and if it is not, that is a prerequisite row in dependsOn, never a narrowed DoD.

FIX SHAPE: in readReleaseDossierInput (release-durable-facts.ts:89-114) consume the same criterion-evidence seam goal closure uses, bind per-criterion evidence to the release sha, and extend DossierGapCode with e.g. CRITERION_NOT_VERIFIED_AT_SHA so rowOf (release-dossier.ts:96-122) emits a gap when no PASSED criterion receipt exists at the released artifact. At minimum also route receipt.sha through the ancestry predicate in landingOf/rowOf. Keep the pure core data-only (fixtures + golden in release-dossier.test.ts) and let the durable reader do the store reads, matching the existing split. Do NOT add a preview-required refusal; leave the preview section render-only as the DONE rows task-70a7ccd3 / task-2a345b2e designed it.

Also: gates-compose-journey.test.ts:13-15 claims "ORDERING IS PROVEN BY REFUSAL" but no arm asserts Gate 3 before Gate 2 refuses; under the owner direction that header is simply wrong and should be reworded, not made true. A malformed copy of this row (task-4e7e9f24, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A dossier built from nodes whose verifier receipt sha is NOT an ancestor of the release sha lists a gap naming that node (the probe that returned gaps=0 at HEAD now returns a gap), asserted by gap CODE.

A dossier for a goal with an approved criterion that has NO PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact lists a gap by the new DossierGapCode; a goal whose criteria all carry a PASSED receipt at that artifact lists none. Both arms assert the code, and the new code is added to every roster that enumerates DossierGapCode (grep the SHAPE, not the symbol).

The release reader consumes the SAME criterion-evidence seam goal closure consumes (currentCriterionReceipts / readIntegratedCriterionArtifact), proven by a set-equality arm over the receipts each side reads for one fixture goal — no reimplemented authority in release/.

NO preview-required refusal is added: release-decide-contracts.ts's closed code map stays at its three codes plus any evidence code, and an arm proves release.decide with a REJECTED or absent preview decision is still decided on evidence alone (the owner direction of 2026-09-09). The preview section remains rendered verbatim.

The planning architect records in planningNotes the measurement of whether criterion-runner is actually triggered in the normal journey at HEAD; if it is not, a prerequisite producer row is filed and named in dependsOn before this row's plan is submitted.
gates-compose-journey.test.ts header no longer claims ordering is proven by refusal for the Gate 2 -> Gate 3 edge; the :140-143 arm is kept and its intent documented as the unattended path.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted, and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXIT 0 if any dossier section text or gap code the Release card renders changed.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE TWO DEFECTS AND THE PREREQUISITE. NO EDITS.

THIS ROW IS GATED. dependsOn names task-b2b4550835f14b6ebd4a742e1f3b01cf ("Criterion verification runs without a human ADMIN command"), filed while planning this row because DoD 5's measurement came back negative: the criterion runner is composed but NOT triggered in the normal journey. Confirm it reached DONE via get_context.epicSiblings before touching anything. Binding release evidence to criterion receipts while those receipts need two ADMIN commands would make an unattended release IMPOSSIBLE rather than better-evidenced.

DEFECT ONE, read it verbatim at release-dossier.ts:110-112 inside `rowOf`:
`const receiptGaps = receipt === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_ABSENT", ...)] : receipt.sha === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN", ...)] : [];`
A present, non-null receipt sha yields ZERO gaps and never reaches `ancestry()`. Compare `landingOf` at :84-93, which DOES call `ancestry(node.landingSha)` and emits LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR / LANDING_UNMEASURABLE. That asymmetry is the filing's probe: a dossier whose verifier receipt sha is not an ancestor of HEAD returns gaps=0.

DEFECT TWO: nothing under apps/daemon/src/release/ imports `currentCriterionReceipts` or `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact`. Confirm with a grep; the only non-test consumers are http/document-coverage-criteria.ts:27 and criterion-evidence/criterion-service.ts. release-durable-facts.ts reads each node's GENERAL verifier receipt (`receipt.execution.test`, ONE command per node) plus the landing receipt. Per-node is not per-criterion, which is why fixing defect one alone is not enough.

READ THE SEAM YOU WILL CONSUME, so you do not reimplement it: criterion-read.ts:29-44 `currentCriterionReceipts` (latest run COMPLETED, sameCriterionArtifact, receipt PASSED, approved-check and criterionDigest match) and criterion-artifact.ts:34-61 `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` (binds every node landing to the integrated sha via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, checks verifier `workspaceBinding.root`). goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts:24-33 consumes it as GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED — that is the standard this row is raising release to.

CENSUS THE GAP-CODE ROSTER BY SHAPE, NOT BY SYMBOL. `DossierGapCode` is declared at release-dossier-sections.ts:14-22 with seven codes, and `GAP_SENTENCES` at :45 is a `Readonly<Record<DossierGapCode, string>>`, so typecheck forces a sentence for a new code. A full-tree grep for the code literals and GAP_SENTENCES returns exactly five files, all under apps/daemon: gates-journey-fixtures.ts, release-dossier-sections.ts, release-dossier.ts, release-dossier.test.ts, release-evidence-completeness.test.ts. Confirm that list is still exactly those five.

ANCESTRY THE RECEIPT SHA (release-dossier.ts) — the smaller half, and it closes the filing's probe.

In `rowOf` at :110-112, a receipt whose sha is present must go through the same `AncestryPredicate` that `landingOf` already applies to the landing sha. A receipt sha that is NOT an ancestor of the released sha is evidence taken from a tree that is not the one being released, and today it reads as clean.

Re-use the existing vocabulary rather than minting more: `landingOf` at :84-93 already distinguishes NOT_ANCESTOR from UNMEASURABLE and formats the detail as `` `${GAP_SENTENCES[code]} (${sha})` ``. Follow that shape exactly so two releases stay diffable, which release-dossier-sections.ts:10-12 says is why rows are sorted in the first place.

KEEP THE CORE PURE. `rowOf` and `landingOf` are data-only; `ancestry` is injected. Do not reach for a store or a git call here — the durable reader supplies the predicate, and the golden in release-dossier.test.ts depends on that split.

Do not change RECEIPT_ABSENT or RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN. This step adds a check for a case that currently produces NO gap; it re-classifies nothing that already gaps.

CONSUME THE CRITERION SEAM GOAL CLOSURE CONSUMES (release-durable-facts.ts, release-dossier-sections.ts, release-dossier.ts) — the half that makes the dossier mean what it says.

(1) ADD ONE CODE to `DossierGapCode` at release-dossier-sections.ts:14-22 for "this criterion has no PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact" — the filing suggests CRITERION_NOT_VERIFIED_AT_SHA. Add its sentence to `GAP_SENTENCES` at :45; the exhaustive `Record<DossierGapCode, string>` will fail typecheck until you do, which is the guard working.

(2) READ THE EVIDENCE IN THE DURABLE READER, `readReleaseDossierInput` at release-durable-facts.ts:89-114. Call `currentCriterionReceipts` and `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` — the SAME functions goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts consumes. Do NOT reimplement their rules in release/: `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` binds node landings to the integrated sha with `merge-base --is-ancestor` and checks the verifier's `workspaceBinding.root`, and a second copy would drift from the one goal closure trusts. That drift is the disagreement this row exists to end.

(3) EMIT THE GAP IN THE PURE CORE. `rowOf` gains the new gap when the criterion has no PASSED receipt at the released artifact. Keep the reader doing store reads and the core doing data, matching the existing split.

(4) The new code must reach every roster step 1 censused. `GAP_SENTENCES` is enforced by typecheck; gates-journey-fixtures.ts and release-evidence-completeness.test.ts are NOT, so check them by hand.

DO NOT TOUCH release-decide-service.ts:151-163. `releaseDossierGaps` is already the only evidence gate, so a new gap code flows to the refusal with no change there — confirm that by reading rather than by editing.

THE ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3, 4), each asserting a gap CODE rather than a count.

(a) RECEIPT ANCESTRY, release-dossier.test.ts — a dossier built from nodes whose verifier receipt sha is NOT an ancestor of the release sha lists a gap NAMING that node, asserted by code. This is the filing's probe, which returned gaps=0 at HEAD; it must now return a gap. Add the mirror arm too: an ancestor receipt sha still lists none, so the check cannot be a blanket.

(b) CRITERION AT SHA, release-dossier.test.ts — a goal with an approved criterion that has NO PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact lists the new code; a goal whose criteria all carry a PASSED receipt at that artifact lists none. Both arms assert the code (DoD 2).

(c) SET EQUALITY, release-durable-facts.test.ts — the release reader and goal closure read THE SAME receipts for one fixture goal, asserted as set equality over the receipts each side reads (DoD 3). Assert against the production surfaces, never against a helper that reimplements them; a helper-backed arm would pass while the two sides drifted, which is the whole failure this row is about.

(d) NO PREVIEW GATE, release-decide-service.test.ts — `release.decide` with a REJECTED preview decision, and again with NO preview decision, is still decided on evidence alone. Assert that release-decide-contracts.ts's closed code map still holds its three codes plus the evidence code, and that the preview section still renders verbatim. This is the OWNER's direction of 2026-09-09 overruling the external reviewer, so the arm exists to stop a well-meaning future edit reversing it.

Every arm names its expected code and, where two layers could answer, which one did (project rail 1).

CORRECT A FALSE HEADER, THEN THE GATES AND THE ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 6, DoD 7).

(1) THE HEADER, gates-compose-journey.test.ts:13-15. It claims "ORDERING IS PROVEN BY REFUSAL" for the Gate 2 -> Gate 3 edge and NO arm asserts that Gate 3 before Gate 2 refuses. Under the owner direction that claim is simply wrong, so REWORD IT — do not make it true by adding an ordering refusal, which would be the preview gate DoD 4 forbids arriving through a side door. Keep the :140-143 arm and document its intent as the unattended path.

(2) GATES. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0, and "0 passed" is exit 0 too. Run `pnpm typecheck` as well — `GAP_SENTENCES` is an exhaustive Record over the code union, so typecheck is a real guard here.
DoD 7's control-room leg is CONDITIONAL: step 1's shape grep found no gap-code enumerator under apps/control-room, so run it only if you changed dossier section text or a gap code the Release card renders — and say which, rather than running it as a formality or skipping it silently.
If a leg reds at a path this row does not own, attribute it with the path-attributed baseline and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it.

(3) COMPLETION RECORD: state that DoD 5 was discharged at PLANNING time by measurement, with the prerequisite filed as task-b2b4550835f14b6ebd4a742e1f3b01cf and named in dependsOn. Put the arm-by-arm table in a row COMMENT — the completion summary truncates silently at 2000 characters.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: can a dossier now report zero gaps while some criterion has no evidence at the released tree — what path reaches that? Does the new gap fire for a goal with NO approved criteria at all, and is that the right answer or a false alarm? Does consuming the criterion seam make the dossier read the store twice for the same fact, and can those two reads disagree mid-release? Did the receipt-ancestry check change the outcome for any EXISTING fixture, and if so is that a fixture that was quietly wrong? And the question the row is named for: is the evidence at release now at least as strong as the evidence goal closure demands — name the clause on each side that makes it so.

comments.content:
FOLLOW-UP FROM task-f7d38f752b074dc89da30631783aae04 (no-effect landings and goal progress). Not a request to change scope — a decision you may want to read before your release-evidence arms harden.

THE DECISION, recorded on that row by architect-ed42e60a and implemented this session: a node whose landing refused NOTHING_TO_COMMIT ran, was accepted by review, and provably had no bytes to commit. It COUNTS as a landing at every goal-progress gate, contributing NO SHA. Gates that COUNT landings count it; gates that BIND a sha SKIP it, exactly as they already skip a node with no landing at all. Every OTHER refusal (GIT_COMMIT_FAILED, GIT_INDEX_LOCKED, anything decided after the lander journaled its intent to commit) still counts for nothing. The discriminator is the refusal CODE, sound because node-lander.ts:208-210 mints NOTHING_TO_COMMIT before commitJournaledLanding at :223.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PATH YOU OWN. `apps/daemon/src/release/release-durable-facts.ts:46` reads
  && landed.receipt.verifierReceiptId === receipt.receiptId && landed.receipt.outcome === "COMMITTED"
per node. Under the decision above, a NOTHING_TO_COMMIT node should CONTRIBUTE NO LANDING SHA to the dossier rather than be treated as a GAP that withholds it. Measured at HEAD 380cd3ad this session: that file is tracked and CLEAN, and I did not touch it — the seam is yours, not mine, and I am not editing it from another row.

WHAT LANDED THIS SESSION, so you can reuse it rather than re-derive it: `apps/daemon/src/repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts` now exports the shared constant `LANDING_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT` and the one-line predicate `landedWithNoEffect(receipt: LandingReceiptV1): boolean`. The three gates I fixed all call that single predicate so the rule cannot drift between them; if you take this up, please call it too rather than spelling a fourth string comparison. The three fixed seams are criterion-evidence/criterion-artifact.ts (integrated artifact), repository/goal-landing-facts.ts (publish/release offer) and repository/publication-goal-integration.ts (publish prerequisite).

TWO SEAMS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNFIXED, both filed as comments on task-f7d38f75 rather than as rows: preview/preview-goal-landing.ts:84 still demands ALL nodes COMMITTED (its test file is an untracked peer WIP, so editing it would collide), and control-room goal-publish.tsx:65,:70 still says "No node of this goal is landed as a commit yet" for a no-effect goal (cosmetic, control-room lane).

`const receiptGaps = receipt === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_ABSENT", ...)] : receipt.sha === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN", ...)] : [];`
A present, non-null receipt sha yields ZERO gaps and is NEVER passed to `ancestry()`. THE GAP-CODE ROSTER AND EVERY ENUMERATOR (shape grep, not symbol grep, per the rail). `DossierGapCode` is declared at release-dossier-sections.ts:14-22 with SEVEN codes. Two structural enumerators: the union itself, and `GAP_SENTENCES: Readonly<Record<DossierGapCode, string>>` at :45 — an exhaustive Record, so TypeScript FORCES a sentence for a new code, which is a real guard rather than a convention. FILE SIZES, all under the cap: release-durable-facts 114, release-dossier 210, release-dossier-sections 142, release-decide-contracts 112.
